column2: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

“There are four [traits]: whoever has them is a hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; when he disputes, he transgresses; and when he makes a covenant, he betrays it.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
“Is a pure hypocrite”: in hypocrisy of action.
Khaṣlah (“a trait”): with fatḥah on the khāʾ; a characteristic.
Yadaʿahā (“he gives it up”): he leaves it.
Ḥaddatha (“he speaks”): he reports about past events.
“When he makes a promise”: of good,
akhlafa (“he breaks it”): he does not keep it.
Fajara (“he transgresses”): he deviates from the truth in the dispute and uses stratagems to reject it.
Ghadara (“he betrays it”): he breaks the covenant.
A warning against taking on these foul traits, to which the roots of minor hypocrisy go back—hypocrisy of action—which is that a person shows a righteous exterior
while concealing what is contrary to it.
As for major hypocrisy, it is that a person shows belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, while concealing what contradicts all or some of that.
This is the hypocrisy that existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in censure of whose people the Qurʾān was revealed, and it informed us that they are in the lowest depth of the Fire.
Urging soundness of speech, action and intention; for speech is corrupted by lying, intention by breaking promises, and action by betrayal.
